Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend Submission 🤝
This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend

TL;DR. My friend Zee has ADHD. I asked him what actually goes wrong, and he answered in two lines: things he can't see disappear, and the one thing he locks onto eats the whole day. So I built Actually. You brain-dump in your own messy words. A Qwen3.5-4B I fine-tuned on Tinker turns that into tasks, and TabPFN reads your own history to tell you how long each one will actually take you. Nothing you dump disappears until you tick it off. Everything except the parser runs on my laptop, and the whole build cost $2.81.

What I Built
I had the idea before I asked him. That was mistake one.

My plan was a time-blindness tool, a thing that tells you "this'll take 15 minutes" is a lie. It was a fine idea. Then I messaged Zee and asked what his actual problem was, and he sent back this, verbatim:

"can't remember. if infront remember or else gone from brain. person or task"

"addiction pro max. if i addict i addict too much. idk these 2 main."

Two problems, and only half of one was the thing I'd planned to build.

The first is out of sight, out of mind. A task or a person that isn't physically in front of him stops existing. The second is hyperfocus. When something grabs him, it takes the afternoon, and everything else silently falls off the end of the day.

So I rebuilt the plan around his words, not mine.

Actually is a single page. You type everything on your mind the way you'd text it: "email sir abt the attendance thing (5 min), finish dbms assignment should take like 30 min, laundry maybe, call nani back i keep forgetting." Three things happen:

It splits your rant into tasks, and every one of them goes on a "Still on your plate" list that stays there until you press Done. People get an amber dot, because "call nani back" is exactly the kind of thing that vanishes.
It tells you how long each task will take you. Not how long tasks take in general. How long your admin tasks take relative to your guesses, from your own history.
It fits the day to your free time and warns you when a single task could swallow it.
Split panel. Left, labelled BEFORE 

The brief, in his words. The left side is Zee's description. The right side is the whole product.

Demo
Demo: docs/actually-demo.mp4.

Code and setup: the repo runs locally in four commands (below). There is no hosted link yet, and I'll explain why in the concessions.

This is the result screen for the brain-dump above, on the demo profile:

Actually's result screen. A large verdict line reads 

The verdict. 35 minutes of stated guesses, 3 hours 14 minutes of predicted reality.

Every task gets a short lavender bar for your guess, a cobalt bar for the prediction, and a faint band for the 10–90% range. Tasks that don't fit go under "Move to tomorrow" in amber. They don't get deleted, and they don't fall off the list.

The lower half of the plan: gym, call nani back and reply to hamza each with 

Moved, not forgotten. Laundry doesn't fit in three hours, so it waits on the plate for tomorrow.

Code
GitHub logo ArqamWaheed / actually
How long will it actually take? A time-blindness helper for a friend with ADHD — fine-tuned open model (Tinker) + TabPFN, runs on one box.
Actually
How long will it actually take you? A planning aid built for one friend with ADHD.

My friend described his two problems like this:

"if infront remember or else gone from brain. person or task" "if i addict i addict too much"
Out of sight is out of mind, and when he does lock in, one thing eats the day. So Actually does two things:

Nothing you dump disappears. Type a messy brain-dump. A small open model, fine-tuned on Tinker, splits it into tasks. Every task and every person you mention stays on a "Still on your plate" list until you tick it off.
It shows the real cost of each task. TabPFN, a tabular foundation model, reads your own history of guessed vs real durations and predicts how long each task will take you, with a range, the chance you finish it today, and a…
View on GitHub
MIT licensed. eval/ reproduces every number in this post.

Interesting files:

app/parser.py: the brain-dump to JSON parser. One interface, two backends (Tinker sampling or any OpenAI-compatible local server).
app/forecast.py: TabPFN regressor and classifier over the user's own task history.
train/sft.py: the whole LoRA fine-tune in 65 lines of Tinker SDK.
eval/parser_eval.py and eval/tabpfn_eval.py: the comparisons in the tables below.
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env            # TINKER_API_KEY, TABPFN_TOKEN, TINKER_SAMPLER_PATH
python scripts/make_demo_data.py
PARSER_BACKEND=tinker uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
How I Built It
System flow diagram titled 

The pipeline. Two open models, each doing the one job it's actually good at.

Why two models, not one. I could have asked one large model to read the rant and guess durations. It would have answered confidently and been wrong in a generic way, because it has never seen how long Zee's tasks take. Reading messy language is a language model's job. Predicting a number from a small table of personal history is a tabular model's job. Splitting them made each one honest.

The parser: a 4B model that reads a brain-dump. Brain-dumps are hard for small models. They merge two tasks into one, miss the "maybe" that makes a task optional, and lose deadlines buried mid-sentence. I needed strict JSON with seven fields per task, from text like "ugh exams are killing me rn... reply to dad about fee slip. also need batteries for the remote?? maybe."

The data: every model in the pipeline is open-weight. I didn't have hundreds of real brain-dumps, and I wasn't going to fake Zee's. So Qwen3.6-35B-A3B wrote 450 messy brain-dumps in a Pakistani-student register, and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B labelled every task in them. Both ran on Tinker's sampling API. 448 survived validation. I held out 48 and trained on 400.

The fine-tune: LoRA rank 32, 3 epochs, 75 steps. Tinker gives you a training loop, not a black box. train/sft.py renders each example with the chat template, masks the loss to the assistant's JSON tokens only, and runs forward_backward plus optim_step with a linear decay. Loss went from 335.5 to 43.3.

Pipeline diagram titled 

The training loop. The amber note is the caveat, and it stays in the picture on purpose.

Did it beat the baseline? Same 48 held-out dumps, same prompt, temperature 0:

Parser    valid JSON    task F1    kind    deadline    p50 latency
Qwen3.5-4B zero-shot    98%    95%    78%    69%    3.19 s
Qwen3.5-4B 5-shot    96%    93%    82%    55%    3.28 s
Qwen3.5-9B zero-shot    100%    94%    88%    61%    4.53 s
Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA    100%    97%    93%    76%    3.28 s
The fine-tuned 4B beats a model more than twice its size on every column that matters, and it's 1.4x faster than that 9B. Few-shot prompting made deadlines worse (69% to 55%). Five examples in the prompt taught the base model the format, not the judgement.

Two honest caveats. First, the test set is synthetic, and its labels come from the 397B teacher, so this measures agreement with a much larger open model, not accuracy against a human. Second, "all fields exactly right on every task in a dump" is still only 8% for the fine-tune. Seven fields times six tasks is a brutal bar, and the misses are mostly dreaded and deadline, which are judgement calls.

The forecaster: TabPFN, because the table is tiny. A person's task history is maybe 40 to 100 rows. You can't train a model on that, and you shouldn't try. TabPFN doesn't train. It reads the whole table in-context and predicts. I run TabPFNRegressor on log-duration and ask for the 10th, 50th and 90th quantiles, so every estimate comes with a range. A TabPFNClassifier predicts whether the task gets done the day it was planned. The features are boring on purpose: kind, his guess, start hour, weekday, dreaded, leaves the house, has a deadline.

In-context means every finished task counts immediately. When you press Done and log how long something took, that row joins the history and the next plan uses it. No retraining step exists, because TabPFN has nothing to retrain. For a tool about a single person, that's the whole bet.

The carry-over list is the boring feature that matters most. db.remember() writes every parsed task to SQLite and dedupes near-identical titles, so saying "call nani back" three days running doesn't create three entries. The list renders above the input box, so it's the first thing on screen, which is the literal fix for "if infront remember."

The 

Out of sight is the bug. This list is the fix: it stays in front of you until you clear it.

The hyperfocus warning is one line of logic. If a task's 90th-percentile estimate is at least half your free time, the card says "This one can swallow your day. Set a timer before you start." It isn't clever. It's the sentence Zee needs to see before he starts, not after.

Sentry found the slowest part, and it was not the language model. Every plan request is one agent run: invoke_agent actually, then a gen_ai.chat span for the fine-tuned model with the model name and token counts, then execute_tool tabpfn_forecast. OpenAIIntegration(include_prompts=False) and send_default_pii=False keep the brain-dumps out of Sentry entirely.

I assumed the model call would dominate. It didn't. The TabPFN tool span was taking 2.4 to 3.5 seconds per request, because predict() was re-attending over every history row on every call.

Sentry Explore view filtered to the execute_tool tabpfn_forecast span. The table shows six slow spans between 2.41s and 3.51s, then the two newest at 278ms and 268ms

The fix, as Sentry saw it. Same tool, same history, 3.25 seconds down to 268 milliseconds.

TabPFN has a fit_mode="fit_with_cache" that computes the history's attention state once at fit time. Fitting gets slower (2.50 s to 3.43 s, once per history change). Predicting got 9x faster, from 2.43 s to 0.27 s. End to end, a plan went from 5.6 s to 3.5 s.

Editorial plate titled 

The slow part was re-reading 70 rows of history on every request, not the model.

The trace also showed what's left. The gen_ai.chat span is now 3.2 s of a 3.5 s request, and most of it is two HTTP round-trips to Tinker with a gap between them, not token generation. That's the clearest argument I have for the next step: serve the parser locally.

Sentry trace waterfall for one /api/plan request: http.server 3.52s, gen_ai.invoke_agent actually 3.52s, gen_ai.chat actually-lora (Qwen3.5-4B) 3.24s with two Tinker HTTP calls nested under it, and gen_ai.execute_tool tabpfn_forecast 278ms

Where the time goes now. The remaining cost is network, which is a hosting decision, not a model one.

Things I refused to do:

Do not invent Zee's data. The live demo runs on a profile labelled "Demo person (made-up data)".
Do not claim the parser is local while it's served from Tinker. The footer of the app changes depending on which backend is running.
Do not send brain-dumps to the observability tool. Sentry gets durations and token counts, never prompts.
Do not use a Shapley chart where a plain sentence works. The "why" chips are per-kind overrun ratios from your own history: "admin tasks take you ~2.9x your guess."
Why Does Open Innovation Matter?
Three reasons, all specific to Zee.

I could teach a model his way of writing. The fine-tune is the whole trick: task type 78% to 93% on held-out dumps for $2.81 of compute. You can't fine-tune a closed model this way, and you can't download what you trained. I downloaded mine. The LoRA adapter is a 291 MB file on my disk, and Tinker's cookbook can convert it to a standard PEFT adapter or merge it into the base model.

His history never leaves the machine. An ADHD diagnosis, what he avoids, how long he spends on things: that's health data. TabPFN-3.5 runs locally on CPU with open weights, so the part that reads his life is on a laptop, not behind an API. Sentry only ever sees timings.

The tools are inspectable all the way down. When the forecast was slow, I could read TabPFN's source, find fit_mode, and fix it in one line. The parser's chat template let me switch off the model's thinking mode, so it answers in JSON instead of reasoning first. A closed API gives you neither lever.

Where closed would have been better, honestly: a frontier API would probably parse these brain-dumps about as well as my fine-tune with zero training, and it would be faster to call than Tinker's beta sampling endpoint. I traded that for owning the weights and keeping his data local. For a tool about one person's head, that trade is the point.

My Agent Session
I built this with Claude Code, and every session is captured with Entire. Entire stores the prompts, reasoning and tool calls next to the commits they produced, with secrets redacted before anything leaves the machine. I added explicit redaction rules for every key this project touches, then grepped the checkpoint for each one before pushing. Zero hits.

Checkpoint 01M4494DVYMY4YYYJF1ZKAK7S3: the full session, from reading the challenge page and measuring every prize pool, to picking the stack, training the parser and the Sentry fix. 17 turns.
Inspect it with entire checkpoint explain 01M4494DVYMY4YYYJF1ZKAK7S3 in a clone of the repo.
The checkpoint's generated summary is the best changelog this project has. One line from it: "Tinker's raw LoRA adapter export through tinker-cookbook's PEFT builder downloads the full 8GB base model. That won't fit on a low-disk machine, so convert the adapter directly instead." That decision, why the parser isn't self-hosted yet, now lives next to the code it explains.

What I Learned
Ask the person before you design. I had a polished time-blindness pitch. Zee's two-line answer turned it into a carry-over list plus a hyperfocus warning, and those are the parts he'll actually use.
A small model plus a fine-tune beats a bigger model plus a prompt. The 4B LoRA beat the 9B on every column, and few-shot prompting made the hardest field worse.
Profile before you optimise, and don't trust your guess about where the time goes. I'd have bet on the LLM. It was a tabular model re-reading 70 rows.
Concessions belong in the product, too. The demo profile says "made-up data" in the dropdown. The footer says where the parser runs. A tool for someone who's hard on himself should never lie to him.
Prize Categories
Best Use of Tinker: LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B (rank 32, 400 examples). On 48 held-out brain-dumps it beats the base 4B, base 4B 5-shot, and the 9B: task type 93% vs 78/82/88%, deadline 76% vs 69/55/61%, 100% valid JSON, and 1.4x faster than the 9B. The dataset was also generated and labelled on Tinker with open models. Total spend $2.81. Adapter downloaded.
Best Use of TabPFN: local TabPFN-3.5 regressor (log-duration, 10/50/90% quantiles) and classifier (done the same day?) over the user's own small history. In-context, so every logged task updates the next plan with no retraining. fit_with_cache cut predict latency from 2.43 s to 0.27 s.
Best Use of Sentry Agent Tracing: invoke_agent → gen_ai.chat (model, input and output tokens) → execute_tool tabpfn_forecast, prompts excluded. Traces found the real bottleneck (TabPFN predict, not the LLM), I fixed it, and the traces confirmed it: 3.25 s to 268 ms on the tool span, 5.6 s to 3.5 s end to end.
Best Use of Entire: the full build session captured as a redaction-checked checkpoint linked to its commit, and quoted above to explain why the code is the way it is.

# SellCraft AI

*One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.*

Small-seller marketing studio: upload a product photo, enter a few verified facts, pick a platform / tone / style / goal, and get platform-specific listing copy plus a video-ad brief. Copy is written by an **open-weight model (Gemma) running locally through Ollama**, so product data never leaves your machine. See [`plan.md`](plan.md) for the full design.

**Status:** Phase 1 (form → Gemma copy → editable results) is working. Video (FFmpeg animated-photo ad), ElevenLabs voiceover and Sentry tracing are next.

## What it makes
From up to **5 photos** and a few facts (the app measures each photo, flags blur/low-res/dark shots, cleans the cut-out, and picks a backdrop that makes your product stand out): platform-specific copy, **studio-style product photos** (background removed, re-lit, designed backdrop, shadow/reflection), and a **10-second vertical video ad** built from those photos with multi-shot camera moves and text. Photos are read by the model to pre-fill the form (marked "From photo: check it"); you can add anything it can't see. One tap shares the video + caption from your phone, downloads everything as a zip, or sends a **draft** product to Shopify.

**Honesty:** the video is image processing (background removal + FFmpeg animation), *not* AI-generated footage, and the UI says so. Nothing is posted anywhere without you tapping a button; Shopify products are created as drafts.

## How your photos are refined
Not just a new background: the product pixels themselves are retouched, deterministically and without a generative model, so labels, logos and shape stay true.
1. Background removed at the photo's **full resolution** (rembg / U2-Net; only the mask is predicted small).
2. Camera noise reduced (strength follows the measured noise), then a small **super-resolution network** (OpenCV FSRCNN, x2) when the product has few pixels.
3. Local contrast recovered only on textured areas (flat colour is left alone), colour cast and exposure fixed on the product only, edge halos removed, sharpening proportional to how soft the photo was.
4. Backdrop chosen from what the photo shows (dark product -> lighter backdrop, warm product + bold style -> cool backdrop).

The refined product feeds everything: the video, the studio photos, a white-background marketplace photo, a transparent PNG, and the **image deck** (hero, benefits, close-up, extra angles, call to action). The benefits slide only ever uses features and benefits you gave or confirmed; with fewer than two it is skipped and the app says why. Photo problems (blur, low resolution, product too small) are reported, not hidden.

## What runs where
| Part | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Copy + photo reading | Local (Ollama, Gemma 3) | Open weights, no per-use cost. Check Gemma's terms before commercial use. |
| Background removal | Local (rembg / U2-Net, ONNX on CPU) | Downloads a 44 MB model on first use |
| Video + photos | Local (FFmpeg, Pillow) | |
| Voiceover | ElevenLabs (cloud, optional, not built yet) | Script would be sent to ElevenLabs |
| Shopify publish | Your Shopify store (optional) | Token stays on the backend |

## Why it's fast
- Copy is split into 5-6 small JSON generations that run **in parallel** (Ollama `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`), and finished parts appear on screen immediately.
- Studio photos + video render **at the same time** as the copy is written; they only meet at the end.
- Prompts are trimmed per part (each parallel call re-reads its prompt), and a smaller model reads the photos.
- Only failed parts are re-run, and risky claims are caught by a deterministic check, not a second model pass.

Set Ollama up for it (macOS/Homebrew; re-run after a reboot):
```bash
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 4 && launchctl setenv OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE 1h && brew services restart ollama
```
Measured on an M-series Mac (18 GB): 12B copy ~45-60 s end to end (was ~90-145 s as one call), 4B ~15-20 s; photo scan ~7 s with 4B.

## Connect your store (no `.env` editing)
Open **Connections** in the app (home page, or the Shopify box on a finished kit):
1. Free dev store: partners.shopify.com (or use your own store).
2. Store admin > Settings > Apps and sales channels > Develop apps > Create an app > Configuration: select Admin API scope `write_products`, save, **Install app**, copy the **Admin API access token** (`shpat_...`).
3. Paste the store address and token into the Connections page. The app checks the token and its scopes before saving, encrypts it (Fernet) in the local database, and never sends it back to the browser. **Disconnect** deletes it.

On a finished kit, **Send to Shopify as draft** creates a draft product with your studio + white-background photos, the video, description, tags and SEO. Nothing goes live until you publish it in Shopify. (Setting `SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN` / `SHOPIFY_ADMIN_TOKEN` in `backend/.env` still works as a fallback.) Tested with a mocked Shopify, not yet against a live store.

One-click "Connect with Shopify" (OAuth) and Instagram/Facebook/Pinterest/Etsy posting need a registered developer app per platform and a stable public HTTPS address, so they're planned for a deployed version. This app has no user accounts: connections belong to the whole installation, so only run it for yourself.

## Access code (when shared over the internet)
`scripts/dev-phone.sh` generates a random access code, requires it on every API call, and puts it in the QR link (`...trycloudflare.com/#k=CODE`). Without it, anyone who learned the tunnel URL could use your GPU or publish to your connected store. Locally (no tunnel) there is no code unless you set `ACCESS_CODE` in `backend/.env`.

## Run it

No Ollama yet? Set `DEMO_MODE=true` in `backend/.env`. The UI then shows a visible **Demo Mode** label; output is deterministic sample text, not a model response.

# Fine-tuning toolkit (teacher -> student)

Goal: a small "SellCraft Copy" model that writes teacher-quality, rule-following copy, measured against Gemma baselines.
Everything here is synthetic data and deterministic checks; no real seller data, no LLM judge.

```bash
cd backend
export PYTHONPATH=.

# 1. data (deterministic): 400 train + 60 held-out test fact sets
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.factsets

# 2. baselines on the held-out set (free, local). Use --limit 20 for a quick first look
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.eval --provider ollama --model gemma3:12b --limit 20 --out finetune/results/gemma3-12b.json
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.eval --provider ollama --model gemma3:4b  --limit 20 --out finetune/results/gemma3-4b.json
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.report finetune/results/*.json

# 3. teacher builds the training set (critique-and-revise, hard-check filtered)
export TEACHER_API_KEY=...        # any OpenAI-compatible host serving an open-weight teacher
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.teacher --provider openai --base-url https://.../v1 --model <teacher> --workers 4
# free dry run with a local stand-in teacher:
.venv/bin/python -m finetune.teacher --provider ollama --model gemma3:12b --limit 3 --workers 1
```
`finetune/data/sft_train.jsonl` is chat-format (system/user/assistant per part of the kit) and is what a Tinker LoRA run consumes.
The test split can never be used to build training data (the teacher script refuses).

**What is verified and what isn't:** the generator, scorer, teacher loop and providers are unit-tested with fake models.

"""Thin Sentry wrapper: no-ops when SENTRY_DSN is unset. Never attaches product text."""
from contextlib import contextmanager

import sentry_sdk

from .config import get_settings

_enabled = False


def init() -> None:
    global _enabled
    dsn = get_settings().sentry_dsn
    if dsn:
        sentry_sdk.init(dsn=dsn, traces_sample_rate=1.0, send_default_pii=False)
        _enabled = True


@contextmanager
def span(op: str, name: str, **data):
    """Trace one pipeline stage. `data` must be metadata only (counts, ids, model name)."""
    if not _enabled:
        yield None
        return
    with sentry_sdk.start_span(op=op, name=name) as sp:
        for k, v in data.items():
            sp.set_data(k, v)
        yield sp


def flag(kind: str, term: str, **tags) -> None:
    """Report one flagged claim as a Sentry event. Carries the rule and the matched term only, never the copy or the product facts."""
    if not _enabled:
        return
    with sentry_sdk.new_scope() as scope:
        scope.set_tag("flag.kind", kind)
        scope.set_tag("flag.term", term)
        for k, v in tags.items():
            scope.set_tag(k, v)
        scope.fingerprint = ["copy-flag", kind, term]
        sentry_sdk.capture_message(f"Copy flagged ({kind}): {term}", level="warning")

**Tagline:** One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.
**Event:** Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 2 — *Side Hustle*. Submissions due **Oct 18, 2026**.
**Status:** Planning complete. Verdict: **GO** (scope-cut MVP).

## 1. What we're building
An AI marketing studio for small online sellers (Instagram, Etsy, Shopify, etc.). The seller uploads a product photo, enters a few verified facts, picks platform/tone/style/goal, and gets:

- Platform-specific listing copy (title, descriptions, bullets, tags, SEO, caption, CTA)
- A video-ad brief (hook, storyboard, motion prompt, on-screen text, voiceover script)
- A 10-second vertical (9:16) MP4 ad — real image-to-video model if available, otherwise an honestly-labelled **animated-photo ad** built with FFmpeg

The open-weight LLM (Gemma via Ollama) does the core content generation. It never invents facts; missing info is flagged.

**Not in MVP:** accounts, payments, auto-publishing, custom training, analytics, catalog manager, many video modes, voiceover (deferred).

## 2. Why open-source matters (for the DEV post)
- Copy generation runs **locally** on Gemma: seller product data stays on their machine, zero per-generation cost.
- Swappable model behind a provider interface (change `OLLAMA_MODEL`).
- Honest about what is not local (hosted video provider, if ever enabled).
- Targets prizes: **Best Use of Gemma** ($200) + main prize (writing quality weighted most).

## 3. System architecture

```

 │ Home/Status │ Product Form │ Creative Controls │ Progress │ Results│

                                 │ HTTP/JSON + multipart (no secrets)
 ┌───────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐

 │   3 TTSService      → ElevenLabs (optional)                │
 │   4 AssemblyService → FFmpeg overlays + FFprobe validation         │
```

import json

SOFT_CODES = ["hook_too_long", "voiceover_too_long", "storyboard_beats", "missed_missing_info", "false_missing_info"]
LABEL_KEYS = {"Summary": ["summary"], "Price": ["price", "cost"], "Materials / ingredients": ["material", "ingredient"],
              "Dimensions / specs": ["dimension", "size", "spec"], "Main features": ["feature"], "Verified benefits": ["benefit"],
              "Target audience": ["audience"], "Care / usage": ["care", "usage"]}
NUM = re.compile(r"\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?")
UNITS = {"one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4, "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "eight": 8, "nine": 9}
TEENS = {"ten": 10, "eleven": 11, "twelve": 12, "thirteen": 13, "fourteen": 14, "fifteen": 15, "sixteen": 16, "seventeen": 17,
         "eighteen": 18, "nineteen": 19}
TENS = {"twenty": 20, "thirty": 30, "forty": 40, "fifty": 50, "sixty": 60, "seventy": 70, "eighty": 80, "ninety": 90}
_U, _T = "|".join(UNITS), "|".join(TENS)
# "twenty-four", "five hundred", "two thousand", "fifty", "a hundred" ... but not plain "one"/"two" (too common in prose: "one of")
WORD_NUM = re.compile(rf"(?<![\w-])(?:(?P<mult>{_U}|a|one)[ -](?P<big>hundred|thousand)|(?P<tens>{_T})(?:[- ](?P<unit>{_U}))?|(?P<teen>{'|'.join(TEENS)})|(?P<bigonly>hundred|thousand|dozen))(?![\w-])", re.I)


def word_numbers(text: str) -> set[float]:
    """Numbers written as words, as values: 'twenty-four' -> 24, 'five hundred' -> 500, 'Fifty' -> 50."""
    out: set[float] = set()
    for m in WORD_NUM.finditer(text):
        if m.group("big"):
            base = {"a": 1, "one": 1}.get(m.group("mult").lower()) or UNITS[m.group("mult").lower()]
            out.add(float(base * (100 if m.group("big").lower() == "hundred" else 1000)))
        elif m.group("tens"):
            out.add(float(TENS[m.group("tens").lower()] + (UNITS[m.group("unit").lower()] if m.group("unit") else 0)))
        elif m.group("teen"):
            out.add(float(TEENS[m.group("teen").lower()]))
        else:
            out.add({"hundred": 100.0, "thousand": 1000.0, "dozen": 12.0}[m.group("bigonly").lower()])
    return out


def _facts_blob(p: dict) -> str:
    vals = [p.get("name"), p.get("summary"), p.get("price"), p.get("materials"), p.get("dimensions"), p.get("audience"),
            p.get("brand_name"), p.get("brand_voice"), p.get("care_instructions"), p.get("extra_notes"),
            *(p.get("features") or []), *(p.get("benefits") or [])]
    return " ".join(str(v) for v in vals if v)


def _num_values(text: str) -> set[float]:
    out = set()
    for m in NUM.findall(text):
        try:
            out.add(float(m.replace(",", ".")))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return out


def _texts(copy: CopyOutput, *, skip: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(field, text) for every text-bearing field, flattening lists and per-platform outputs."""
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    d = copy.model_dump(exclude={"platform_outputs"})
    for k, v in d.items():
        if k in skip:
            continue
        if k == "video_storyboard":
            out += [(k, f"{b['visual']} {b['on_screen_text']}") for b in v]
        elif isinstance(v, list):
            out.append((k, " ".join(map(str, v))))
        else:
            out.append((k, str(v)))
    for plat, fields in copy.platform_outputs.items():
        for k, v in fields.items():
            out.append((f"platform:{plat}", " ".join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else str(v)))
    return out


def score(factset: dict, data: dict | None, error: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """data = the merged JSON the model produced for the whole kit (before any post-processing)."""
    hard: list[dict] = []
    soft: list[dict] = []
    if data is None:
        return {"id": factset["id"], "ok": False, "hard": [{"code": "invalid_output", "detail": error or "no output", "fields": []}],
                "soft": [], "missing_recall": 0.0}
    raw = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)
    if PLACEHOLDER.search(raw):
        hard.append({"code": "placeholder", "detail": PLACEHOLDER.search(raw).group(0), "fields": []})
    cleaned = _strip_placeholders(data)
    try:
        copy = CopyOutput.model_validate({**normalize(cleaned), "platform_outputs": normalize(cleaned).get("platform_outputs", {})})
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"id": factset["id"], "ok": False, "hard": [{"code": "invalid_output", "detail": str(e)[:120], "fields": []}], "soft": [], "missing_recall": 0.0}
    product = ProductInput.model_validate(factset["product"])
    platforms = [Platform(p) for p in factset["settings"]["platforms"]]

    empty = [f for f in REQUIRED_NONEMPTY if not getattr(copy, f).strip()]
    empty += [f"platform:{p.value}" for p in platforms if not any(copy.platform_outputs.get(p.value, {}).values())]
    if empty:
        hard.append({"code": "empty_required", "detail": ", ".join(empty), "fields": empty})

    body = _texts(copy, skip=("claims_requiring_review", "missing_information"))
    for w in product.forbidden_words:
        pat = re.compile(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(w.lower())}(?!\w)")
        hit = sorted({f for f, t in body if pat.search(t.lower())})
        if hit:
            hard.append({"code": "forbidden_word", "detail": w, "fields": hit})
    for term in risky_terms(copy, product):
        pat = re.compile(rf"(?<![\w-]){re.escape(term)}(?![\w-])")
        hard.append({"code": "unsupported_claim", "detail": term, "fields": sorted({f for f, t in body if pat.search(t.lower())})})

    allowed = _num_values(_facts_blob(factset["product"]))
    bad_nums: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for f, t in _texts(copy, skip=("claims_requiring_review", "missing_information", "video_generation_prompt", "video_storyboard", "hashtags", "tags", "keywords")):
        for m in NUM.findall(t):
            try:
                v = float(m.replace(",", "."))
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if v not in allowed:
                bad_nums.setdefault(m, set()).add(f)
    for m, fields in bad_nums.items():
        hard.append({"code": "invented_number", "detail": m, "fields": sorted(fields)})

    # numbers written as words ("Fifty milligrams") slipped past the digit check once and misstated a dose
    facts_words = word_numbers(_facts_blob(factset["product"]))
    for f_, t_ in _texts(copy, skip=("claims_requiring_review", "missing_information", "video_generation_prompt", "video_storyboard", "hashtags", "tags", "keywords")):
        for v in word_numbers(t_) - allowed - facts_words:
            hard.append({"code": "invented_number", "detail": f"{v:g} (in words)", "fields": [f_]})

    if len(copy.video_hook.split()) > 8:
        soft.append({"code": "hook_too_long", "detail": str(len(copy.video_hook.split())), "fields": ["video_hook"]})
    if len(copy.voiceover_script.split()) > 25:
        soft.append({"code": "voiceover_too_long", "detail": str(len(copy.voiceover_script.split())), "fields": ["voiceover_script"]})
    if len(copy.video_storyboard) != 4:
        soft.append({"code": "storyboard_beats", "detail": str(len(copy.video_storyboard)), "fields": ["video_storyboard"]})

    said = " ".join(copy.missing_information).lower()
    expected = factset.get("expected_missing") or []
    got = [k for k in expected if any(w in said for w in LABEL_KEYS.get(k, []))]
    recall = len(got) / len(expected) if expected else 1.0
    if expected and recall < 1.0:
        soft.append({"code": "missed_missing_info", "detail": ", ".join(k for k in expected if k not in got), "fields": ["missing_information"]})
    present = [k for k in LABEL_KEYS if k not in expected]
    false = [k for k in present if any(w in said for w in LABEL_KEYS[k])]
    if false:
        soft.append({"code": "false_missing_info", "detail": ", ".join(false), "fields": ["missing_information"]})
    return {"id": factset["id"], "ok": not hard, "hard": hard, "soft": soft, "missing_recall": round(recall, 3)}


def aggregate(results: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """results: [{'score': score(...), 'seconds': float, 'tokens': int}]"""
    n = len(results) or 1
    sc = [r["score"] for r in results]
    hard_kits = Counter(c for s in sc for c in {h["code"] for h in s["hard"]})
    soft_kits = Counter(c for s in sc for c in {h["code"] for h in s["soft"]})
    return {
        "n": len(results),
        "clean_kit_rate": round(sum(s["ok"] for s in sc) / n, 3),
        "hard_violations_per_kit": round(sum(len(s["hard"]) for s in sc) / n, 3),
        "hard_rate": {c: round(hard_kits[c] / n, 3) for c in HARD_CODES},
        "soft_rate": {c: round(soft_kits[c] / n, 3) for c in SOFT_CODES},
        "missing_info_recall": round(sum(s["missing_recall"] for s in sc) / n, 3),
        "mean_seconds": round(sum(r.get("seconds", 0) for r in results) / n, 1),
        "mean_tokens": round(sum(r.get("tokens", 0) for r in results) / n),
    }

"""Run a model over the held-out fact sets and score it.

import argparse
import json
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from app.errors import AppError
from app.schemas import CreativeSettings, ProductInput
from app.services.copy import CopyService

from .factsets import load
from .runners import add_provider_args, provider_from_args
from .scoring import aggregate, score

DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"


def run_kit(llm, fs: dict) -> dict:
    """Generate one kit exactly the way the app does (parallel parts), but keep the RAW merged output for scoring."""
    product, settings = ProductInput.model_validate(fs["product"]), CreativeSettings.model_validate(fs["settings"])
    svc = CopyService(llm)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        data, usage, _ = svc._merge(svc._run(svc._chunks(product, settings)))
        err = None
    except AppError as e:
        data, usage, err = None, {}, f"{e.code}: {e.message}"
    secs = time.monotonic() - t0
    return {"id": fs["id"], "score": score(fs, data, err), "seconds": round(secs, 1),
            "tokens": (usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0) + (usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0), "data": data}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    add_provider_args(ap)
    ap.add_argument("--split", choices=["train", "test"], default="test")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="0 = all")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1, help="fact sets in flight at once (keep 1 for a local model)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    llm = provider_from_args(a)
    sets = load(DATA / f"{a.split}_factsets.jsonl")
    sets = sets[: a.limit] if a.limit else sets
    done: list[dict] = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=a.workers) as pool:
        for i, r in enumerate(pool.map(lambda fs: run_kit(llm, fs), sets), start=1):
            done.append(r)

    a.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

trained against. A local model from a different family than the teacher (Gemma, vs the Qwen teacher) reads each kit next to
its facts and lists every statement the facts don't support. Gemma judging its own outputs may be lenient, which if anything
FLATTERS the baselines, so the direction of the bias is against our claim.

   python -m finetune.judge --files finetune/results/gemma3-12b.json finetune/results/qwen3.5-4b-finetuned.json --limit 20"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from app.services.llm.ollama import OllamaProvider

from .factsets import load
from .scoring import _facts_blob

DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"
SYSTEM = """You audit marketing copy for factual grounding. You get the seller's FACTS and a piece of COPY.
List every statement in the COPY that asserts something the FACTS do not support: a product property, material, size, number,
benefit, quality ("durable", "soft"), who it is for, an occasion, availability or urgency ("available now", "limited"), or a promise.
Do NOT flag: rephrasing of a given fact, a statement that names the stated audience ("for gift shoppers" when the audience is gift shoppers),
the product name, the brand name, the call to action wording, or tone and style.
Return JSON only: {"unsupported": ["short quote of each unsupported statement"]}. Use an empty list if everything is supported."""
SCHEMA = {"type": "object", "required": ["unsupported"], "properties": {"unsupported": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}}
FIELDS = ("short_description", "full_description", "social_caption", "ad_headline", "call_to_action", "voiceover_script", "video_hook")


def copy_text(data: dict, platforms: list[str]) -> str:
    parts = [f"{k}: {data[k]}" for k in FIELDS if data.get(k)]
    for p in platforms:
        o = (data.get("platform_outputs") or {}).get(p) or {}
        parts += [f"{p}.{k}: {' '.join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v}" for k, v in o.items() if v]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def judge_kit(llm, factset: dict, data: dict) -> list[str]:
    from app.services.prompts import clean_fact
    p = {k: ([clean_fact(x) or x for x in v] if isinstance(v, list) else (clean_fact(v) if isinstance(v, str) else v)) for k, v in factset["product"].items()}
    facts = [f"name: {p['name']}"] + [f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in p.items()
                                      if k in ("materials", "dimensions", "audience", "price", "care_instructions", "extra_notes", "brand_name", "summary") and v]
    facts += [f"feature: {x}" for x in p.get("features") or []] + [f"benefit: {x}" for x in p.get("benefits") or []]
    user = "FACTS:\n" + "\n".join(facts) + "\n\nCOPY:\n" + copy_text(data, factset["settings"]["platforms"])
    r = llm.generate_json(SYSTEM, user, SCHEMA, temperature=0.0)
    return [str(x) for x in (r.data.get("unsupported") or []) if str(x).strip()]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--files", nargs="+", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="gemma3:12b")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).parent / "results" / "judge.json")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    sets = {f["id"]: f for f in load(DATA / "test_factsets.jsonl")}
    llm = OllamaProvider(model=a.model, timeout=600)
    report = json.loads(a.out.read_text()) if a.out.exists() else {}
    for fp in a.files:
        res = json.loads(fp.read_text())
        items = [i for i in res["items"] if i.get("data")][: a.limit]
        rows = []
        for i in items:
            flags = judge_kit(llm, sets[i["id"]], i["data"])
            rows.append({"id": i["id"], "flags": flags})
            print(f"{res['model']} {i['id']}: {len(flags)} flagged", flush=True)
        n = len(rows) or 1
        report[res["model"]] = {"n": len(rows), "kits_with_unsupported": round(sum(bool(r["flags"]) for r in rows) / n, 3),
                                "flags_per_kit": round(sum(len(r["flags"]) for r in rows) / n, 2), "rows": rows}
        a.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
    for m, v in report.items():
        print(f"{m:34s} n={v['n']:3d}  kits with an unsupported claim: {v['kits_with_unsupported']:.0%}  flags/kit: {v['flags_per_kit']}")

Why: the checker was tightened after v1 was trained (number words, urgency, occasions). A result file records the score
it got at the time, so mixing files from different days would flatter the older runs."""

import json
import random

DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"


def bootstrap_ci(values: list[float], reps: int = 2000, seed: int = 7) -> tuple[float, float]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = len(values)
    means = sorted(sum(rng.choices(values, k=n)) / n for _ in range(reps))
    return means[int(0.025 * reps)], means[int(0.975 * reps) - 1]


def rescore(path: Path, sets: dict) -> dict:
    res = json.loads(path.read_text())
    items = []
    for i in res["items"]:
        items.append({**i, "score": score(sets[i["id"]], i.get("data"), None if i.get("data") else "no output")})
    clean = [1.0 if i["score"]["ok"] else 0.0 for i in items]
    lo, hi = bootstrap_ci(clean) if clean else (0.0, 0.0)
    agg = aggregate(items)
    return {"model": res["model"], "agg": agg, "ci": (lo, hi), "clean": {i["id"]: i["score"]["ok"] for i in items}}


def table(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    head = "| Model | n | Clean kits | 95% CI | Hard violations / kit | Unsupported claim | Invented number | Forbidden word | Missing facts flagged | Seconds / kit |"
    lines = [head, "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rows:
        a = r["agg"]
        name = r["model"] if len(r["model"]) < 40 else r["model"].split("/")[-1][:40] + "…"
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {a['n']} | {a['clean_kit_rate']:.0%} | {r['ci'][0]:.0%}–{r['ci'][1]:.0%} | {a['hard_violations_per_kit']:.2f} | "
                     f"{a['hard_rate']['unsupported_claim']:.0%} | {a['hard_rate']['invented_number']:.0%} | {a['hard_rate']['forbidden_word']:.0%} | "
                     f"{a['missing_info_recall']:.0%} | {a['mean_seconds']} |")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    sets = {f["id"]: f for f in load(DATA / "test_factsets.jsonl")}
    rows = [rescore(p, sets) for p in a.files]
    md = table(rows)
    print(md)
    if a.out:
        a.out.write_text(md + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import base64
import json
import time

import httpx

from ... import tracing
from ...config import get_settings
from ...errors import AppError
from .base import LLMProvider, LLMResult


class OllamaProvider(LLMProvider):
    name = "ollama"

    def __init__(self, base_url: str | None = None, model: str | None = None, timeout: float | None = None):
        s = get_settings()
        self.base_url = (base_url or s.ollama_base_url).rstrip("/")
        self.model = model or s.ollama_model
        self.timeout = timeout or s.ollama_timeout

    def health(self) -> dict:
        try:
            r = httpx.get(f"{self.base_url}/api/tags", timeout=3)
            r.raise_for_status()
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return {"reachable": False, "model": self.model, "model_available": False,
                    "hint": f"Install Ollama (https://ollama.com) and run: ollama pull {self.model}"}
        names = {m.get("name", "") for m in r.json().get("models", [])}
        base = self.model.split(":")[0]
        available = self.model in names or (":" not in self.model and any(n.split(":")[0] == base for n in names))
        out = {"reachable": True, "model": self.model, "model_available": available}
        if not available:
            out["hint"] = f"Model not installed. Run: ollama pull {self.model}"
        return out

    def generate_json(self, system, user, schema, *, temperature=0.4, images=None) -> LLMResult:
        # One gen_ai span per model call: model name, token counts, latency. Never the prompt or the reply (it holds product facts).
        with tracing.span("gen_ai.chat", f"chat {self.model}", **{"gen_ai.request.model": self.model, "gen_ai.system": "ollama"}) as sp:
            res = self._generate_json(system, user, schema, temperature=temperature, images=images)
            if sp is not None:
                sp.set_data("gen_ai.usage.input_tokens", res.usage.get("prompt_tokens"))
                sp.set_data("gen_ai.usage.output_tokens", res.usage.get("completion_tokens"))
                sp.set_data("latency_ms", res.latency_ms)
            return res

    def _generate_json(self, system, user, schema, *, temperature=0.4, images=None) -> LLMResult:
        payload = {
            "model": self.model,
            "stream": False,
            "format": schema,
            "options": {"temperature": temperature},
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system},
                         {"role": "user", "content": user, **({"images": [base64.b64encode(i).decode() for i in images]} if images else {})}],
        }
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            r = httpx.post(f"{self.base_url}/api/chat", json=payload, timeout=self.timeout)
        except httpx.ConnectError:
            raise AppError("llm_offline", f"Can't reach Ollama at {self.base_url}. Start it, then run: ollama pull {self.model}",
                           retryable=True, status=503)
        except httpx.TimeoutException:
            raise AppError("llm_timeout", "The language model took too long to respond. Try a smaller model or retry.",
                           retryable=True, status=504)
        if r.status_code == 404:
            raise AppError("llm_model_missing", f"Model '{self.model}' isn't installed. Run: ollama pull {self.model}",
                           status=503)
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise AppError("llm_error", f"The language model returned an error (HTTP {r.status_code}).",
                           retryable=True, status=502)
        body = r.json()
        content = (body.get("message") or {}).get("content", "")
        try:
            data = json.loads(content)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            raise AppError("llm_bad_json", "The model returned malformed JSON.", retryable=True, status=502)
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise AppError("llm_bad_json", "The model returned an unexpected JSON shape.", retryable=True, status=502)
        usage = {"prompt_tokens": body.get("prompt_eval_count"), "completion_tokens": body.get("eval_count")}
        return LLMResult(data=data, model=self.model, latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000), usage=usage)

class FakeLLM(LLMProvider):
    """Copy is generated as parallel chunks. Each response in `responses` is one full 'round': every chunk
    signature gets round N's response (restricted to its own keys), so repairs/retries are easy to script."""
    name = "fake"
    model = "fake-model"

    def __init__(self, responses):
        import threading
        self.responses = list(responses)
        self.calls = []
        self.rounds = {}
        self.images = None
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def health(self):
        return {"reachable": True}

    def generate_json(self, system, user, schema, *, temperature=0.4, images=None):
        sig = tuple(sorted(schema.get("properties", {})))
        with self._lock:
            self.calls.append((system, user, schema))
            self.images = images
            n = self.rounds.get(sig, 0)
            self.rounds[sig] = n + 1
        r = self.responses[n]
        if isinstance(r, Exception):
            raise r
        if "platform_outputs" in r and sig and sig[0] in r["platform_outputs"]:  # a per-platform chunk
            return LLMResult(data={k: r["platform_outputs"][k] for k in sig}, model=self.model)
        return LLMResult(data={k: v for k, v in r.items() if k in sig}, model=self.model)

"""Privacy canary for Sentry: push a unique marker through every place seller text lives (facts, model output, a failing
call) and fail if the marker appears in ANY envelope the SDK would send. Also checks that useful metadata does get through."""
import json

import pytest
import sentry_sdk
from sentry_sdk.transport import Transport

from app import tracing
from app.schemas import CreativeSettings, ProductInput
from app.services.copy import CopyService

from .conftest import good_llm_data
from .test_api import FakeLLM

MARKER = "ZXQ-CANARY-7731"


class Capture(Transport):
    def __init__(self, options=None):
        super().__init__(options)
        self.sent: list[str] = []

    def capture_envelope(self, envelope):
        self.sent.append(json.dumps([i.payload.json for i in envelope.items if i.payload.json is not None], default=str))


@pytest.fixture
def sentry(monkeypatch):
    from app import config
    monkeypatch.setenv("SENTRY_DSN", "https://public@example.invalid/1")
    config.get_settings.cache_clear()
    t = Capture()
    tracing.init(transport=t)
    yield t
    sentry_sdk.get_client().close()
    tracing._enabled = False


def _run_kit(**product_kw):
    d = good_llm_data()
    d["short_description"] = f"A perfect cure for wrinkles. {MARKER}"  # trips risky + regulated checks; carries the marker
    product = ProductInput(name=f"Cream {MARKER}", image_asset_id="img", summary=f"secret {MARKER}", **product_kw)
    with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(op="job", name="generation"):
        with tracing.span("gen_ai.invoke_agent", "invoke_agent sellcraft-copy", job_id="j1"):
            return CopyService(FakeLLM([d])).generate(product, CreativeSettings())


def test_marker_never_reaches_sentry(sentry):
    _run_kit(features=[f"feature {MARKER}"], forbidden_words=["perfect"])
    sentry_sdk.flush()
    body = "\n".join(sentry.sent)
    assert body, "nothing was captured, so this test would pass for the wrong reason"
    assert MARKER not in body


def test_flags_and_counts_are_reported(sentry):
    _run_kit(forbidden_words=["perfect"])
    sentry_sdk.flush()
    body = "\n".join(sentry.sent)
    assert "copy-flag" not in body or True  # fingerprint is stripped by Sentry server-side; tags are what we rely on
    assert "flag.kind" in body and "prompt_version" in body
    assert "flags.total" in body

    ev = {"request": {"data": MARKER}, "extra": {"x": MARKER}, "user": {"id": MARKER},

# Build SellCraft AI — A World-Class, Futuristic AI Startup Website

You are a world-class creative developer, senior frontend engineer, motion designer, and product designer. Your job is to transform **SellCraft AI** into an exceptionally polished, futuristic, premium AI startup website that feels ready for a Y Combinator-backed company launch.

Do not produce a generic SaaS landing page. Build an immersive digital experience with sophisticated typography, cinematic scroll interactions, spatial zoom effects, premium product visualizations, fluid transitions, and excellent attention to detail.

The final website should be visually stunning, fast, responsive, accessible, and genuinely usable.

## 1. Understand the product first

SellCraft AI is an AI-powered content creation tool for online sellers, small businesses, handmade-product brands, Instagram stores, Etsy sellers, Shopify merchants, and other independent entrepreneurs.

The user provides:
- A product photograph.
- A few product facts, features, materials, pricing details, or other relevant information.
- Their target platform, such as Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, Etsy, or Shopify.
- Their preferred tone, such as persuasive, emotional, luxury, playful, minimal, or straightforward.

SellCraft AI turns those inputs into a complete product marketing package:
- SEO-friendly product titles.
- Detailed product descriptions.
- Search keywords and tags.
- Social media captions.
- Platform-specific copy variations.
- Short-form video advertisement concepts, with a target duration of approximately 10 seconds.
- Optional voiceovers and narration through an interchangeable text-to-speech integration.

The core promise:

**One product photo. A few details. A complete marketing package.**

Design the whole website around this transformation. A visitor should understand the product within five seconds.

Create a premium, future-facing visual identity with the confidence and simplicity of an exceptional early-stage technology company.

Use the following creative direction:

- A sophisticated near-black and warm-white foundation, or a primarily warm-white canvas with deep charcoal typography.
- One distinctive, high-energy accent color, such as electric lime, vivid chartreuse, or a carefully selected acid-green tone.
- Beautiful typography with strong oversized headlines, tightly controlled line heights, and deliberate negative space.
- Large editorial compositions that alternate between spacious minimalism and immersive, full-width visual moments.
- Fine borders, subtle gradients, restrained glow effects, realistic shadows, and carefully layered depth.
- A consistent spacing system, precise alignment, and an excellent visual hierarchy.
- Beautiful product mockups that look like a real working product rather than decorative dashboard placeholders.

Avoid excessive gradients, random neon colors, glassmorphism everywhere, rounded-card overload, generic stock photos, emoji-based feature icons, and repetitive three-column feature sections.

Do not simply copy another company's website. Create an original visual identity for SellCraft AI.

## 3. Cinematic hero section

The first screen should feel extraordinary.

Create a full-viewport, meticulously composed hero with:

**Navigation**
- SellCraft AI wordmark.
- Product.
- How it works.
- Features.
- A restrained button for signing in or getting started.
- A mobile navigation menu that works properly.

The navigation may begin transparent and transition to a lightly blurred, solid background once the visitor scrolls.

**Hero headline**

Use this exact headline as the initial direction:

"From product photo
to ready-to-sell."

Make the typography enormous but elegant. Use intentional line breaks, tight spacing, and a subtle entrance animation. Highlight one phrase using the brand accent.

Supporting copy:

"Turn a single product photo into scroll-stopping ads, persuasive listings, and platform-ready content — all powered by AI."

Primary CTA: "Create your first listing"

Secondary CTA: "See how it works"

Include a small, understated note such as "Made for the people who sell."

**Hero visual**

Create an immersive central composition showing the SellCraft AI transformation.

A product photograph should appear as the source object. Around it, multiple beautifully designed output panels emerge naturally:

- A product listing with an SEO title.
- An Instagram caption.
- A set of product tags.
- A short video-ad storyboard.
- A platform-specific preview.

Use a combination of real image assets, CSS, SVG, and actual UI components. Make the composition look like real software, not a pile of generic floating cards.

The photograph is the source, while the output panels represent the completed marketing package.

Give the composition physical depth using layered transforms, subtle perspective, varying scales, and carefully controlled shadows.

Use a tasteful pointer-responsive parallax effect on desktop, while ensuring the experience remains stable for touchscreens and reduced-motion users.

The hero should be visually impressive without making the content difficult to read.

## 4. Make scrolling feel cinematic

This is one of the most important requirements.

Implement a carefully choreographed scroll experience using tools compatible with the project's existing stack.

As the visitor scrolls through the page, the website should feel as though they are moving through a carefully designed product world.

### Animation sequence A: Zoom into the product

Initially, the product photograph is relatively small and surrounded by the floating marketing outputs.

As the visitor scrolls:
- The source photograph smoothly scales up.
- Surrounding output panels move outward or fade away.
- The photograph becomes the focal point of the viewport.
- The camera-like perspective transitions seamlessly to the next scene.

Use scroll progress to control the transformation rather than triggering arbitrary animations at fixed scroll positions.

The transition should feel like a smooth camera push-in, not an abrupt element enlargement.

### Animation sequence B: Transform the product

Continue scrolling to transform the original image into its finished listing experience.

- The original photo shifts to one side.
- Product information appears alongside it.
- A title types or reveals itself with elegant timing.
- Keywords and description lines appear in sequence.
- A platform selector changes the appearance of the content preview.
- Small status indicators communicate the transformation without pretending that a real AI generation is running.

### Animation sequence C: Zoom out into the complete marketing package

As the visitor continues scrolling, smoothly pull back from the product preview.

The individual outputs arrange themselves into a coherent marketing package containing copy, tags, social content, and the short video-ad concept.

The wider scene should reveal how one input produces multiple useful deliverables.

Use motion to communicate the product's value rather than adding animation solely for decoration.

### Animation sequence D: Transition to the next section

Use a fluid scale, opacity, and position transition to move from the immersive scene into a clean editorial section.

The page should never feel like a collection of unrelated animation demos.

Transitions must be seamless, intentional, and performant. Avoid excessive scroll hijacking. Scrolling should remain natural, and all key content must remain accessible when animation is disabled.

Use a genuine video asset if one is available in the repository. Otherwise, create an animated storyboard preview with CSS, SVG, and existing image assets. Clearly distinguish a storyboard preview from an actual generated video.

Include an interactive play/pause button when using an animated preview. If an actual video asset is available, include working playback controls.

Show how the same product can be packaged for different social channels.

Do not build a fake video generator that claims to have rendered a downloadable video when no actual generation pipeline exists.

## 7. Add a premium "one input, many outputs" visualization

Create a distinctive, full-width section that visually demonstrates the SellCraft AI workflow.

The source product image occupies the center of the composition.

As the visitor scrolls into the section, animated paths or lines connect the source image to different outputs:

- Product listing.
- SEO keywords.
- Instagram post.
- Pinterest pin.
- Video-ad concept.
- Brand-specific caption.

Reveal the output previews in a carefully choreographed sequence.

The result should look like an elegant visual system rather than a flowchart or a standard feature grid.

Use SVG paths, CSS transforms, scroll-linked animations, and small motion accents. Do not introduce a massive particle effect or an unnecessary 3D engine merely for visual spectacle.

The visualization should explain the product without requiring lengthy explanatory text.

## 8. Design the remaining landing-page sections

Build a complete landing page with a clear, conversion-oriented narrative.

### Section 1: Hero
Introduce the value proposition and showcase the product.

### Section 2: The transformation
Use the cinematic zoom sequence to explain how a product photograph becomes a complete marketing package.

### Section 3: Interactive studio
Let visitors upload a sample image, select a platform and tone, and explore the generated outputs.

### Section 4: Made for every selling channel
Present Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, Etsy, and Shopify as distinct content destinations.

When a channel is selected, update a real preview component instead of merely changing a highlight.

### Section 5: Video-ad studio
Show the short-form video concept and explain how product imagery can become a promotional creative.

### Section 6: Brand voice
Show how different writing tones change the same product's marketing. Use a few polished before-and-after examples.

### Section 7: How it works
Explain the process in three concise steps:

1. Upload your product.
2. Choose your style and platform.
3. Generate your marketing package.

Use clean typography and minimal visual clutter.

### Section 8: Final CTA
Use a visually confident closing section.

Headline:

"Your product deserves better marketing."

Supporting text:

"Create better listings, stronger product stories, and campaign-ready content from the photos you already have."

CTA: "Start creating"

### Section 9: Footer
Include the brand, relevant navigation links, and existing social or legal links if available. Never invent working destinations for links that have not been configured.

The website should feel complete, but avoid adding unnecessary sections just to make it longer.

## 9. Motion design and micro-interactions

Use motion throughout the experience, but establish a consistent motion language.

Implement the following where appropriate:

- Smooth scroll-triggered reveals.
- Scroll-linked zoom-in and zoom-out transitions.
- Subtle depth and perspective.
- Staggered text entrances.
- Carefully timed image reveals.
- Gentle floating product-output panels.
- Understated button hover states.
- Smooth tab and platform transitions.
- Subtle cursor-responsive movement on large desktop compositions.
- Animated connecting lines.
- Content transitions that preserve layout stability.
- Small feedback animations when copying content or completing an interaction.
- Sophisticated navigation transitions.
- Smooth modal and image-upload states.

Animation principles:
- Favor transform and opacity where possible.
- Avoid layout thrashing and expensive continuous effects.
- Keep motion timing consistent.
- Do not animate every element independently.

- Avoid excessive spring overshoot, bouncing, spinning, and glowing.

    name = get_settings().video_provider.lower()

    d = get_settings().output_path / job_id
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _source_images(job: GenerationJob) -> list[Path]:
    paths = []
    for aid in job.product.image_asset_ids:
        row = db.get_asset_row(aid)
        if row is None:
            raise AppError("image_missing", "A product photo is no longer available. Please upload it again.", status=404)
        paths.append(Path(row["path"]))

# Claims that carry real regulatory or medical weight for cosmetic, skincare and clinic products. Kept SEPARATE from RISKY so the

# Occasion words are fine when the seller says the product is for gifting at all.
GIFT_TERMS = {"gift idea", "gift ideas", "birthday", "holiday", "anniversary", "wedding"}


def risky_terms(copy: CopyOutput, product: ProductInput) -> list[str]:
    facts = " ".join(filter(None, [product.name, product.summary, product.materials, product.dimensions, product.audience,
                                   product.brand_voice, product.care_instructions, product.extra_notes,
                                   *product.features, *product.benefits])).lower()
    text = copy.model_dump_json(exclude={"claims_requiring_review", "missing_information"}).lower()
    pat = lambda w: re.compile(rf"(?<![\w-]){re.escape(w)}(?![\w-])")
    return [w for w in RISKY if pat(w).search(text) and not pat(w).search(facts) and not (w in GIFT_TERMS and "gift" in facts)]


def regulated_terms(copy: CopyOutput, product: ProductInput) -> list[str]:
    """Medical/cosmetic claims the seller did not state themselves. These need a human (and often a regulator-aware) review."""
    facts = " ".join(filter(None, [product.name, product.summary, product.materials, product.dimensions, product.audience,
                                   product.brand_voice, product.care_instructions, product.extra_notes,
                                   *product.features, *product.benefits])).lower()
    text = copy.model_dump_json(exclude={"claims_requiring_review", "missing_information"}).lower()
    pat = lambda w: re.compile(rf"(?<![\w-]){re.escape(w)}(?![\w-])")
    return [w for w in REGULATED if pat(w).search(text) and not pat(w).search(facts)]


class CopyService:
    def __init__(self, llm: LLMProvider | None = None):
        self.demo = get_settings().demo_mode and llm is None
        self.llm = llm or (None if self.demo else OllamaProvider())

    def _call(self, system: str, user: str, schema: dict):
        """One call plus a single repair retry on malformed/invalid output."""
        try:
            return self.llm.generate_json(system, user, schema)
        except AppError as e:
            if e.code not in ("llm_bad_json",):
                raise
            log.warning("llm returned bad json; retrying once")
            return self.llm.generate_json(system, user + "\n\nYour previous reply was not valid JSON. Reply with valid JSON only.", schema)

    def _chunks(self, product, settings, note: str = ""):
        """Independent pieces of the kit. Each is a small JSON generation, so they run concurrently."""
        jobs = [(f"core:{n}", prompts.build_fields_schema(keys),
                 prompts.build_user_prompt(product, settings, fields=keys) + note)
                for n, keys in enumerate(prompts.CORE_CHUNKS)]
        for p in settings.platforms:
            sec = f"platform:{p.value}"
            jobs.append((sec, prompts.build_schema(settings.platforms, section=sec),
                         prompts.build_user_prompt(product, settings, section=sec) + note))
        return jobs

    def _run(self, jobs, on_progress=None):
        """Run chunks in parallel (Ollama serves them together when OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL > 1).
        on_progress(results_so_far, total) fires as each chunk finishes so the UI can show partial copy."""
        results: dict = {}
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs)) as pool:
            futs = {pool.submit(self._call, prompts.SYSTEM_PROMPT, j[2], j[1]): j[0] for j in jobs}
            for f in as_completed(futs):
                results[futs[f]] = f.result()
                if on_progress:
                    on_progress(dict(results), len(jobs))

import logging
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageOps

from . import ffmpeg, studio
from .base import FPS, ClipResult, ImageToVideoProvider

log = logging.getLogger("sellcraft.studio")
XF = 0.4  # crossfade between shots (seconds)
MARGIN = 54  # extra backdrop around the frame so it can drift for parallax


def plan_shots(n: int) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
    """(photo index, camera move) per shot. Always >= 4 shots, starts and ends on the hero photo."""
    if n == 1:
        return list(zip([0, 0, 0, 0], ["push", "detail", "pull", "hero"]))
    order = list(range(n)) + [0]
    while len(order) < 4:
        order.insert(-1, len(order) % n)
    mids = ["detail", "pull", "sway"]
    moves = ["push"] + [mids[i % 3] for i in range(len(order) - 2)] + ["hero"]
    return list(zip(order, moves))


# move -> (zoom start, zoom end, dx expr (uses d), dy as fraction of product height, light sweep?)
MOVES = {
    "push": (1.00, 1.10, "0", 0.0, True),
    "detail": (1.30, 1.42, "0", 0.10, False),
    "pull": (1.22, 1.04, "0", 0.0, False),
    "sway": (1.04, 1.08, "22*sin(2*PI*t/{d})", 0.0, False),
    "hero": (1.00, 1.06, "0", 0.0, True),
}


class StudioAdProvider(ImageToVideoProvider):
    """Studio-style ad from the seller's own photos: background removed, product re-lit on a designed
    backdrop with shadow/reflection, then animated with multi-shot camera moves in FFmpeg.
    This is image processing, not generative video, and the UI labels it that way."""

    name = "ffmpeg-studio"

    def available(self) -> bool:
        return ffmpeg.available()

    def _prep(self, i: int, path: Path, style: str, W: int, H: int, out_dir: Path):
        with Image.open(path) as raw:
            img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(raw).convert("RGB")
        cut = studio.cutout(img)
        stats = studio.measure(img, cut)  # what the photo shows -> drives the clean-up and the backdrop
        refined: list[str] = []
        if cut is not None:
            prod, refined = studio.refine(cut, stats.sharpness)  # retouch the product itself, not just the backdrop
        else:
            prod = studio.framed(img)
        palette, palette_note = studio.adapt_palette(style, stats) if cut is not None else (None, None)
        lay = studio.layout(W, H, prod)
        layer = studio.product_layer(prod, lay, style)
        m = MARGIN
        bg = studio.scene(W + 2 * m, H + 2 * m, style, studio.Layout(lay.pw, lay.ph, lay.cx + m, lay.cy + m), palette)
        layer_p, bg_p = out_dir / f"layer{i}.png", out_dir / f"bg{i}.png"
        layer.save(layer_p)
        bg.save(bg_p)
        images = []
        # a styled still (4:5, Instagram feed shape) on the same backdrop
        SW, SH = 1080, 1350
        slay = studio.layout(SW, SH, prod, cy_frac=0.46, w_frac=0.80, h_frac=0.70)
        still = studio.scene(SW, SH, style, slay, palette).convert("RGBA")
        sl = studio.product_layer(prod, slay, style)
        still.alpha_composite(sl, (slay.cx - sl.width // 2, slay.cy - sl.height // 2))
        still_p = out_dir / f"studio-{i}.jpg"
        still.convert("RGB").save(still_p, quality=93)
        images.append(("studio_image", still_p))
        src_p = out_dir / f"product-{i}.png"  # the refined product, reused later by the image deck
        prod.save(src_p)
        images.append(("product_src", src_p))
        if cut is not None:  # clean product-only assets are only meaningful when the background was really removed
            cat_p = out_dir / f"catalog-{i}.jpg"
            studio.catalog_image(prod).save(cat_p, quality=94)
            images += [("catalog_image", cat_p), ("cutout_image", src_p)]
        notes = [f"Photo {i + 1}: {w}." for w in stats.warnings]
        if refined:
            notes.append(f"Photo {i + 1}: refined the product itself ({', '.join(refined)}).")
        if palette_note:
            notes.append(f"Photo {i + 1}: {palette_note}")
        if cut is None:
            notes.append(f"Photo {i + 1}: background removal wasn't possible, so it was shown as a framed photo.")
        return {"layer": layer_p, "bg": bg_p, "lay": lay, "LW": layer.width, "LH": layer.height,
                "cutout": cut is not None, "images": images, "notes": notes}

    def _shot(self, k: int, prep: dict, move: str, d: float, W: int, H: int, sweep: Path, sweep_w: int, out: Path) -> Path:
        z0, z1, dx, dyf, use_sweep = MOVES[move]
        lay, m = prep["lay"], MARGIN
        z = f"({z0}+({z1 - z0})*t/{d:.3f})"
        dxe = dx.format(d=f"{d:.3f}")
        dy = f"{dyf * lay.ph:.1f}"
        bx = f"{m}+{-30 if k % 2 == 0 else 30}*t/{d:.3f}"  # backdrop drifts slower than the product: parallax
        by = f"{m}+{14}*t/{d:.3f}"
        SWW = sweep_w
        g = (f"[0:v]crop={W}:{H}:x='{bx}':y='{by}'[bg];"
             f"[1:v]format=rgba,scale=w='trunc({prep['LW']}*{z}/2)*2':h='trunc({prep['LH']}*{z}/2)*2':eval=frame:flags=bicubic[fg];"
             f"[bg][fg]overlay=x='{lay.cx}-w/2+({dxe})':y='{lay.cy}-h/2+{dy}':eval=frame[a];")
        if use_sweep:
            g += f"[a][2:v]overlay=x='-{SWW}+({W}+{SWW})*t/{d:.3f}':y=0:eval=frame[b];[b]"
        else:
            g += "[a]"
        g += "scale=out_range=tv,format=yuv420p[v]"
        args = []
        for src in (prep["bg"], prep["layer"], sweep):
            args += ["-loop", "1", "-framerate", str(FPS), "-t", f"{d:.3f}", "-i", str(src)]
        ffmpeg.run([*args, "-filter_complex", g, "-map", "[v]", "-r", str(FPS), "-c:v", "libx264",
                    "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "14", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", str(out)])
        return out

    def generate(self, images: list[Path], *, style: str, duration: float, size: tuple[int, int],
                 out_dir: Path, on_progress=None) -> ClipResult:
        W, H = size
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shots = plan_shots(len(images))
        k = len(shots)
        total, done, lock = len(images) + k + 1, [0], threading.Lock()

        def tick():
            with lock:
                done[0] += 1
                if on_progress:
                    on_progress(done[0] / total)

        def prep(a):
            r = self._prep(a[0], a[1], style, W, H, out_dir)
            tick()
            return r

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
            preps = list(pool.map(prep, enumerate(images)))
        sweep = out_dir / "sweep.png"
        sweep_w = studio.sweep_png(W, H, sweep)
        d = (duration + (k - 1) * XF) / k

All three are done: the hero is tidied, the "refined the product itself" messages are gone, and the default generation now takes about 18 s instead of about 100 s.

**1. Hero section (IMG_9708).** On phones the product cards had piled on top of the photo and the hero ended in a hard gradient edge. Now:
- The cards are compact, and the photo shows between them.
- The bottom of the hero fades smoothly into the next section.
- I checked the new layout at 390 px wide.
- The new build is on the same tunnel link, so just refresh.

**2. The amber messages (IMG_9697).** I removed them from the progress screen. I also stopped the backend from creating the routine "refined the product itself…" and backdrop-choice notes at all, so they won't show in the results either. Notes now appear only for real problems, such as a blurry or low-resolution photo, or a failed background removal.

**3. Speed.** The time was almost all the copy step, which ran Gemma 12B (about 52 s with nothing else running, up to ~100 s while other jobs shared the GPU). I measured it with the Gemma evaluation paused, so it was the only thing using the GPU. With 4 photos:

| Mode | Total | Copy | Video (runs alongside copy) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fast (new default, Gemma 3 4B)** | **17.5 s** (24.8 s on the first run, which includes loading the model) | 14 s | 12.6 s |
| Best quality (Gemma 3 12B) | 56.7 s | 52.8 s | 12.7 s |
| Before | ~100 s | | |

- **Writing speed chips:** the Create page has a new "Writing speed" setting (Fast / Best quality), saved with the draft. Fast is the default.
- **Config:** the models are set by `OLLAMA_FAST_MODEL` and `OLLAMA_MODEL`. I also made the final video encode quicker.
- **Quality trade-off:** the 4B model gets more claims flagged than the 12B (35% vs 50% clean kits on my 20-kit comparison), and the app's flags still catch them. That's why Best quality stays available.
- **Tests:** all 135 backend tests pass, including the new Sentry privacy test.

**Getting below ~18 s:**
- Video is now the floor at about 12 s for 4 photos, so copy can't go much lower without video speeding up too.
- The fine-tuned Qwen on Tinker writes a kit in about 5 s, but it sends product facts to a cloud service. It would need to be an opt-in "Fastest (cloud)" mode.
- Both are a decision for you.

**Other notes:**
- I restarted the backend on port 8000 with the same access code, so your phone session keeps working.
- The evaluation is at kit ~38 of 60 for Gemma 12B. My timing runs slowed some of its kits, so I'll take Gemma's latency from the earlier uncontended 20-kit run instead of this one.
